This commit is unreviewable.  You've got a design in mind so you put together some infrastructure that isn't even being used.  Please merge this at least into one commit that uses the infrastructure.

As written, I have no idea why we are creating a virtual class and prefer we do not.

I agree that the commit in its current form doesn’t tells the usage of the infrastructure.

DiscoveryProtocol (Abstract Class)

  discoverDevices(): std::vector<ResponderInfo> = 0

  getType(): TransportType = 0

Concrete Implementations

   MCTPDiscoveryProtocol

   TCPDiscoveryProtocol

   PCIEDiscoveryProtocol
  (All inherit from DiscoveryProtocol)

SPDMDiscovery (Context)

   SPDMDiscovery(std::unique_ptr<DiscoveryProtocol>)

   discover(): bool


By following this design, adding a new transport simply requires creating a new class that inherits from DiscoveryProtocol. No changes are needed in the SPDMDiscovery class.

let me know your thoughts on this
I am implementing the Strategy Design Pattern to make the transport layer easily extensible.
At what point do you intend to have unit tests?  There isn't a single unit test in this entire stack.

We will add it in the later commits, We have it in the downstream but I am just breaking and making the modification to align with the merged design and start using the libspdm, We have our own libspdmd but we are migrating to start using the dmtf libspdm.
Added in the later commits

eid is specific to mctp transport. We need to have abstraction for this in MCTP responder object.
Same as above. uuid is specific to mctp transport. We need to have abstraction for this in MCTP responder object.

We are not using type anywhere, i think we can remove this. Or it's added for any future scope?

wrapping issue.

don't think eid is a common field across transports. it's an mctp specific attribute.

tcp has ip address, and pcie DOE has something like BDF address. we should not generalize this in common infrastructure.

Agree, and It needs to be enhanced when we bring other responders.
Currently it is only MCTP responder
But this should be part of the common discovery code , mctp eid should be in the mctp_transport_discovery.
why do we need the UUID ? do we expose this anywhere ?
When the mCTP endpoint is discovered, we obtain its UUID and EID. We then need to associate the SPDM responder object with the corresponding inventory object using the UUID.
Acknowledged
dont see pcie binding spec at https://www.dmtf.org/standards/spdm. where is this defined ?
Eevn I don't see it but libspdm supports it https://github.com/DMTF/libspdm/tree/3e973c58a594dfa6cf0bc7e53af37cce02cd544a/library/spdm_transport_pcidoe_lib
Acknowledged
do we plan to do discovery over all the transports by default ?
No. Look at the line no 27, Diacovery protocol instance is spdm::MCTPTransportDiscovery

Yeah , but what i meant is does every needs to have all the discoveries enabled by default ? for example if pcie is enabled by someone - does he also need to have mctp discovery code triggered as well (but probably just with no mctp endpoints) ?

No, it depends on the use case. For example, on a platform where we want discovery over both MCTP and TCP, we need to perform discovery through both channels. This behavior can be controlled through the Meson configuration.

If a platform requires discovery only through MCTP, then only MCTP discovery should be enabled. If it requires both, enable both. By default, only MCTP discovery is enabled.
